record.context_brief: cpsd-rank of the average mixing matrix
record.original_question: Compute the completely positive semidefinite rank of the average mixing matrix Mc. Here the completely positive semidefinite rank of a completely positive semidefinite matrix M is the smallest dimension d such that M is the Gram matrix of positive semidefinite matrices of size d x d.

evidence.quote: The completely positive semidefinite rank (cpsd-rank) of a completely positive semidefinite matrix M is the smallest dimension d so that M is the Gram matrix of positive semidefinite matrices of size d × d.
4.3 Open Problem. Compute the cpsd-rank of Mc.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $G$ be a finite simple graph on $n$ vertices with adjacency matrix $A$, and let $A = \sum_{r=0}^{d} \lambda_r E_r$ be its spectral decomposition, where $\lambda_0,\dots,\lambda_d$ are the distinct eigenvalues of $A$ and $E_r$ is the orthogonal projection onto the $\lambda_r$-eigenspace. The continuous-time quantum walk on $G$ is governed by the unitary $U(t) = \exp(itA)$, and its mixing matrix at time $t$ is $M(t) = U(t) \circ \overline{U(t)}$, where $\circ$ denotes the entrywise (Hadamard/Schur) product. The average mixing matrix of $G$ is defined by
$$\widehat{M} \;=\; \lim_{T \to \infty} \frac{1}{T} \int_0^T M(t)\, dt \;=\; \sum_{r=0}^{d} E_r \circ E_r.$$
A symmetric matrix $M \in \mathbb{R}^{n \times n}$ is called completely positive semidefinite (cpsd) if there exist a positive integer $d$ and positive semidefinite matrices $P_1,\dots,P_n \in \mathbb{S}^d_+$ such that $M_{ij} = \operatorname{tr}(P_i P_j)$ for all $i,j$. The completely positive semidefinite rank (cpsd-rank) of such a matrix $M$, denoted $\operatorname{cpsd\text{-}rank}(M)$, is the smallest such dimension $d$. The matrix $\widehat{M}$ is known to be cpsd.

Problem: Determine $\operatorname{cpsd\text{-}rank}(\widehat{M})$ as a function of the graph $G$ (in particular, give exact values or sharp bounds for natural families of graphs).

No subsequent work resolving the cpsd-rank of the average mixing matrix in general was found in the search; related literature (e.g., on cpsd-rank lower bounds and on the average mixing matrix) addresses bounds and structural properties but not a complete computation.
